definitions.explanation: Overwhelming, destructive power, especially of natural disasters, epidemics, or other forces beyond human control. Almost always used with を振るう (to rage, to wreak havoc).

examples.japanese: {台風|たいふう}が{猛威|もうい}を{振|ふ}るった。
examples.english: The typhoon raged with devastating force.

examples.japanese: インフルエンザが{全国|ぜんこく}で{猛威|もうい}を{振|ふ}るっている。
examples.english: Influenza is raging across the entire country.

examples.japanese: {記録的|きろくてき}な{大雪|おおゆき}が{猛威|もうい}を{振|ふ}るい、{交通機関|こうつうきかん}が{完全|かんぜん}にストップした。
examples.english: Record-breaking heavy snow raged and public transportation came to a complete halt.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost exclusively used in the fixed phrase {猛威|もうい}を{振|ふ}るう (to rage, to wreak havoc). Rarely appears outside this collocation. Subjects are typically natural disasters ({台風|たいふう}, {地震|じしん}), diseases (インフルエンザ, ウイルス), or other destructive forces.
This word is a bound noun — it almost never appears alone without を{振|ふ}るう. Learning the full phrase is more useful than learning the word in isolation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {猛威|もうい}を{振|ふ}るう (to rage, to wreak havoc)
- {猛威|もうい}をふるい{続|つづ}ける (to continue raging)
- {自然|しぜん}の{猛威|もうい} (the fury of nature)
